Hi Dylan,

Thanks — the times look reasonable in principle, but our calendars are showing conflicting labels which is causing the team confusion: when you sent the first invite my Google Calendar rendered the slot as 2026-12-14 10:00 JST (good) but Liam in Singapore sees 08:00 SGT (not 09:00), and Sophie in Sydney sees the event as 11:00 AEST on 2026-12-15 (next day).

To be clear: our Tokyo team is OK for 10:00 JST. We just need one consistent invite that doesn't roll to the following day in Sydney. Sophie mentioned that her Outlook/Exchange tenant sometimes displays AEST (UTC+10) rather than AEDT (UTC+11), which explains the one-hour difference and the date rollover.

Can you confirm the UTC offsets you intend to send? If you could send an ICS specifying the timezone explicitly (Asia/Tokyo, Asia/Singapore, Australia/Sydney), that would help.

Regards,
Keiko

Thanks for the quick note, Keiko — good catch and sorry for the calendar churn.

Short answer: I will resend region-specific invites and include explicit TZ IDs and UTC offsets. Here’s the authoritative mapping I’m locking in:

Authoritative times (final):
- 2026-12-14 09:00 SGT (UTC+08:00) — Asia/Singapore
- 2026-12-14 10:00 JST (UTC+09:00) — Asia/Tokyo
- 2026-12-14 12:00 AEDT (UTC+11:00) — Australia/Sydney (note DST in effect)

Why this happened: our first ICS generator emitted "floating" times (no TZ ID) and a handful of Exchange tenants resolve those to local offsets (AEST vs AEDT) which can flip the displayed hour and, in edge cases, the calendar date. To avoid that I will: 1) create three separate calendar events with TZ IDs, and 2) attach a short ics-debug.ics you can inspect if your IT team wants to confirm the TZ block.

I attached a CSV (apac-demo-times.csv) and the debug ICS in case your calendar admin wants to see the payload. If everyone is fine with the AEDT slot for Sydney I’ll send three invites now. If Sophie requests AEST specifically (no DST) we can instead pick a UTC-neutral slot that avoids the rollover (e.g., 00:00 UTC / 09:00 SGT / 10:00 JST / 19:00 AEDT — but that pushes Sydney late).

Next steps: I will send separate invites within 15 minutes. Please confirm if anyone needs an alternate date.

Thanks —
Dylan

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: APAC ICS quirk for PacificGrid demo (FYI / action)

Olga / Maya — quick internal note while I resend invites to the prospect. Keiko reported mixed renders across Exchange / Google: some clients show AEST (UTC+10) and others AEDT (UTC+11). Our ICS generator is currently outputting VTIMEZONE with a TZID but the EVENT DTSTART is floating (no TZ parameter). That is causing tenant clients to interpret offsets differently.

Can you check two things for the Redwood calendar microservice:
- Ensure VEVENT DTSTART/DTEND include TZID parameters (e.g., DTSTART;TZID=Australia/Sydney:20261214T120000) instead of floating times.
- Confirm the VTIMEZONE block includes DST rules for Australia/Sydney for 2026 so clients read the correct offset.

If you need me to forward the prospect's ICS that showed the issue I can attach it. I plan to send three explicit invites (one per TZ) in ~10 minutes.

—Dylan
